draft.title: Measures of centre
card: Mean
Add all the values, then divide by how many there are. Every value affects the mean.
Median
The middle value when the data is in order. With an even number of values, it is the mean of the two middle values.
Mode
The value that occurs most often.
Outliers

An outlier is a value far from the rest. It pulls the mean towards it, but the median barely moves. So the median is a better centre for skewed data or data with outliers. Example: 2, 3, 4, 5, 36 has mean 10 and median 4.
draft.remember: The mean is pulled by extreme values. The median is not, so it suits skewed data.

a.q: What is the median of the data set 7, 3, 9, 4, 12, 5?
a.why: In order the data is 3, 4, 5, 7, 9, 12. There are six values, so the median is the mean of 5 and 7, which is 6. The mean of all values is 6.7, but that is not the middle value.
a.clue: Put the values in order first.

b.q: Five workers at a small firm in Ballarat earn $50 000, $52 000, $54 000, $56 000 and $288 000. Which statement is correct?
opts: The median of $54 000 describes a typical worker better
The mean of $100 000 describes a typical worker better
The mean and median are equal, so either one works
The mode of $50 000 is the best centre, as it is lowest
b.why: The $288 000 value is an outlier. It pulls the mean up to $100 000 (500 000 ÷ 5), which is more than four of the five workers earn. The median of $54 000 is not affected much by the outlier, so it is a better centre.
b.clue: Which value is far from the rest, and which measure does it pull?

b.best: The median of $54 000 describes a typical worker better

problems.detail: The remember line says the median is not pulled by extreme values, but the card says it 'barely moves'. The remember line states it more absolutely than the card does.

Median

Mode

a.why: In order the data is 3, 4, 5, 7, 9, 12. There are six values, so the median is the mean of 5 and 7, which is 6. Taking 9 and 4 from the unordered list gives 6.5, which is wrong because the values were not put in order first.
a.clue: Put the values in order first.

The mode of $50 000 is the best centre, as it is lowest
b.why: The $288 000 value is an outlier. It pulls the mean up to $100 000 (500 000 ÷ 5), which is more than four of the five workers earn. The median of $54 000 barely moves because of the outlier, so it is a better centre, and no value repeats, so there is no mode.
b.clue: Which value is far from the rest, and which measure does it pull?
